boxes.meaning: keep an eye on, look after

english.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for watching over or keeping an eye on someone or something.
Use this as the all-purpose casual choice when you mean keeping an eye on people or a task.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for keeping an eye on and supervising people or activities.
Use 睇住 when you mean keeping an eye on or guarding a person or belonging.
Use 睇住 when “look” means to see to something or keep watch to make sure it is handled.

examples.english: I’m going to take a shower; can you monitor the pot for me?
examples.traditional: 我去沖涼，你幫我睇住個煲。
examples.jyutping: ngo5 heoi3 cung1 loeng4 nei5 bong1 ngo5 tai2 zyu6 go3 bou1

examples.english: Can you supervise the children while I go get some water?
examples.traditional: 你幫我睇住啲細路，我去買杯水。
examples.jyutping: nei5 bong1 ngo5 tai2 zyu6 di1 sai3 lou6 ngo5 heoi3 maai5 bui1 seoi2

examples.english: Can you oversee the kids for me while I go buy a drink?
examples.traditional: 你幫我睇住班細路，我去買杯飲品。
examples.jyutping: nei5 bong1 ngo5 tai2 zyu6 baan1 sai3 lou6 ngo5 heoi3 maai5 bui1 jam2 ban2

examples.english: You watch my bag for me while I go shopping.
examples.traditional: 你幫我睇住個袋，我去買嘢。
examples.jyutping: nei5 bong1 ngo5 tai2 zyu6 go3 doi6 ngo5 heoi3 maai5 je5

examples.english: Can you look after the stove for me?
examples.jyutping: nei5 bong1 ngo5 tai2 zyu6 go3 lou4 fo2
